sections.title: Brazil: Lula Wins a Fourth Term
sections.summary: Lula takes 51.8% in a polling upset; Flávio Bolsonaro seeks annulment; Brazilian assets slide

paragraphs.heading: Upset victory
paragraphs.body: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won Sunday's runoff with about 51.8% of valid votes to Flávio Bolsonaro's 48.2%, a margin of roughly 4.4 million votes, NPR and The Rio Times reported. CNN said he is the first Latin American president to win a fourth term. Most polls had shown Bolsonaro narrowly ahead. Lula takes office for the new term on January 5, 2027. [[TAG:success:fourth term]]

paragraphs.heading: Bolsonaro rejects result
paragraphs.body: Bolsonaro told supporters in Brasília it is 'impossible to recognize the election result' and said he will ask courts to annul it, objecting to a Supreme Court order that kept polling stations open two extra hours, ABC Australia and CNN reported. Both campaigns had sought extensions for different regions. Analysts said the margin makes an annulment unlikely but warned his refusal could spark protests. [[TAG:warning:no concession]]

paragraphs.heading: Market reaction
paragraphs.body: A Tokyo-listed Brazil equity ETF fell nearly 15% and the real was set to weaken sharply, XTB reported; CNBC said investors had positioned for a Bolsonaro win, and XTB attributed much of the drop to traders unwinding those bets. Reports of the US-listed EWZ's overnight move ranged up to about 20%. [[TAG:danger:Brazil ETF -15%]]

sections.title: Iran: Waiting on Trump
sections.summary: Trump rules out a Sunday strike but keeps 'finish them off' option; regional envoys head to Tehran

paragraphs.heading: No strike, yet
paragraphs.body: Trump told reporters 'There will not be a strike today' as he left for Michigan, while saying he is weighing a deal against action to 'finish them off', The National and CBS News reported. Al Jazeera reported CENTCOM has strike plans ready. Officials view the period after the midterms as especially risky. [[TAG:warning:decision pending]]

paragraphs.heading: Tehran's line
paragraphs.body: Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei said no Iranian accepts the 'complete surrender' Washington demands, but that the diplomatic window is open and messages are passing through intermediaries, the AP reported via ABC News and the Times of Israel. An IRGC-affiliated outlet said no new US proposal had been made.

paragraphs.heading: Regional mediators
paragraphs.body: Saudi Defense Minister Khalid bin Salman, Pakistani army chief Asim Munir and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin are traveling to Tehran for regional security talks with Iranian officials, Anadolu and Al Jazeera reported; NBC News said delegations were meeting in Iran. A Saudi official said they would also meet President Masoud Pezeshkian. [[TAG:info:Tehran talks]]

paragraphs.heading: Hormuz
paragraphs.body: CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper flew over the strait and said its primary transit routes 'remain free and clear of Iranian sea mines', The Hill and the Times of Israel reported. The International Maritime Organization says mine and attack risks persist. A US intelligence memo reported by Axios said Iran has stepped up plots against US officials.

sections.summary: Riyadh airport partly reopens after 15 days; Houthis claim a strike on it within hours

paragraphs.heading: Airport reopens
paragraphs.body: Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport partly reopened on Sunday after being shut since an October 10 attack that killed 13, CGTN and The Hans India reported. The Houthis claimed a missile strike on it hours later and warned airlines and travelers it is 'unsafe'; Flightradar24 data showed little traffic, Business Recorder reported. [[TAG:warning:airport targeted]]

paragraphs.heading: Interceptions
paragraphs.body: The Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed 12 missiles and two drones fired at the kingdom, with debris injuring two people, Anadolu reported. The US has ordered non-emergency staff out of Saudi Arabia.

sections.title: Israel Votes Tuesday
sections.summary: Deadlocked polls before Tuesday's election; Hebron operation displaces about 2,670, PA says

paragraphs.heading: The election
paragraphs.body: Israel holds its first national vote since the October 7, 2023 attack on Tuesday, Al Jazeera and NPR reported. A polling average puts Netanyahu's coalition at about 50 seats, short of 61, with Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar leading in eight of nine final polls. Thirty-seven lists are running against a 3.25% threshold, and CNN said the outcome may take weeks to resolve. [[TAG:info:vote Tuesday]]

paragraphs.heading: Hebron operation
paragraphs.body: After Friday's attack that killed two soldiers, Israeli forces demolished homes and detained dozens in Hebron; the Palestinian Authority said about 2,670 people have been displaced, the Times of Israel and The New Arab reported. Netanyahu said forces will apply the 'offensive model' used in refugee camps. The figures could not be independently verified. [[TAG:danger:thousands displaced]]

sections.title: Ukraine and Russia
sections.summary: Zelensky says Kyiv got 24 Patriot interceptors in three months; strikes kill four in Dnipropetrovsk

paragraphs.heading: Patriot appeal
paragraphs.body: Zelensky urged partners to unblock Patriot deliveries European countries had already approved, saying Ukraine needs about 350 interceptors a month but received only 24 in three months, ABC News and The New Voice of Ukraine reported. He said Russia fired about 1,600 guided bombs, 48 missiles and nearly 2,300 drones in a week. [[TAG:danger:24 interceptors]]

paragraphs.heading: Strikes
paragraphs.body: Russian strikes on Dnipropetrovsk region killed four people and injured 22, and in Kharkiv Russia struck a hypermarket and then hit emergency crews responding, ABC News reported. The Kremlin said it would be ready to resume trilateral talks after November 4, the Kyiv Independent reported.

sections.title: Markets: Week Ahead
sections.summary: Fed decides Wednesday; Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon report; Brent eases toward $114.50

paragraphs.heading: Fed and Big Tech
paragraphs.body: The Fed announces its rate decision Wednesday and is widely expected to hold, with CME FedWatch showing about a 90.6% chance of no change, CMC Markets reported. Microsoft and Alphabet report October 28 and Amazon later in the week, in the busiest week of earnings season, with 179 S&P 500 companies reporting, Forbes said. Third-quarter GDP and September PCE inflation are also due. [[TAG:info:Fed Wednesday]]

paragraphs.heading: Oil and Asia
paragraphs.body: Brent fell about 2.2% to $114.52 and WTI to about $101 in early Asian trading on hopes of US-Iran de-escalation, while the UAE's Murban grade rose above $118, Gulf News reported. Asian stocks were mixed, with reported moves varying by source.

sections.title: US Politics
sections.summary: Trump and Obama trade rallies in Michigan's Senate battleground; Trump attacks El-Sayed

paragraphs.heading: Port Huron
paragraphs.body: Trump rallied about 3,000 people in Port Huron for Senate nominee Mike Rogers and gubernatorial candidate John James, defending the Iran war and gas prices, The Detroit News reported. Michigan Advance reported he called Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed a 'jihadist', claims it described as unsubstantiated. [[TAG:warning:anti-Muslim rhetoric]]

paragraphs.heading: Obama in Detroit
paragraphs.body: A day earlier, Barack Obama rallied more than 4,300 people in Detroit with El-Sayed and gubernatorial nominee Jocelyn Benson, calling the midterms the 'last best chance' to check the administration, Bridge Michigan and CBS Detroit reported. Bridge Michigan described the Senate race as a toss-up. [[TAG:info:toss-up]]

sections.title: Europe
sections.summary: Portugal clears housing protest camps; storms cut power to 150,000 homes in northern Europe

paragraphs.heading: Portugal
paragraphs.body: Police cleared housing protest camps in Lisbon's Rossio Square and in Porto before dawn Sunday, arresting 31, Reuters reported via Al Jazeera and Portugal Resident. Police counted 11 injured; activists said about 60. It was the second clearance in a week. [[TAG:warning:protest camps cleared]]

paragraphs.heading: Storms
paragraphs.body: Storms Austen and Boelo cut power to about 150,000 homes and disrupted flights and ferries from Scotland to Denmark, Euronews reported.
